subject: apple seeds
title: What If You Ate the Apple Seeds?

scenes.text: What if you ate the apple seeds? They do contain cyanide. That's not the twist.
Each seed holds a chemical called amygdalin, locked inside a hard shell.
Swallow seeds whole and the shell usually carries them straight through you, untouched.
Chew them, and amygdalin turns into hydrogen cyanide, about 0.6 milligrams per gram of seeds.
A few chewed seeds won't hurt you. Your body clears small doses of cyanide.
To get dangerous, an adult would have to chew and swallow hundreds. One man died after eating a whole cupful.
